reason: The passage describes the people of Israel complaining and quarreling with Moses and the LORD (וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה - 'the people quarreled with Moses'; וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה - 'the people complained against Moses'). While Moses expresses distress to God about the situation (מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לָעָם הַזֶּה - 'What shall I do for this people?'), this is a plea for divine assistance rather than the Hebrew leaders formally complaining about the people. The elders (זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) are mentioned but are passive witnesses to the miracle, not active complainers.
